newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Albania's Berisha says will stay on-interview.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha says will stay on-interview.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha was quoted on Wednesday as saying he was not prepared to relinquish power and that he would not step down until his people voted him out.

"The majority of people in this country are behind me. I am a democratically elected president and will stay on until the people don't want me any more," the embattled leader said in an interview with Austrian current affairs magazine News released ahead of publication on Thursday.
"Never, never will I leave my office."

Albania was plunged into chaos when a string of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes failed earlier this year and armed rebels took control of southern Albania during an unchecked spree of looting and banditry.

Berisha said he was confident an international military force, designed to protect aid deliveries to the ravaged country and expected to become operational next week, would help to restore public order.
"The presence of the international troops will have a big psychological effect on the people in my country, with their help it will be possible to restore public order," he said.

Berisha, who came to power in 1992, admitted it had been his biggest mistake not to rein in the pyramid funds which started to blossom across Europe's poorest nation after the fall of its hardline stalinist regime in 1991.
"The pyramid games were the most negative aspect of our completely liberal economic policy, they caused the collapse," he said.
But he added it was the main opposition Socialists who were to blame for the chaos that had engulfed Albania.

"The Socialists have pushed us into this situation. They spread hatred, acted like bandits, excluded themselves from political life in Albania. Their style created the climate of intolerance that has now led to the explosion," he said.
The Socialist Party on Wednesday returned to Albania's parliament nearly a year after it abandoned its seats following a general election widely condemned as rigged.
The Socialists joined Berisha's Democrats and eight smaller parties in an emergency all-party government last month.
